subject: Logic
title: De Morgan's Laws
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: De Morgan's Laws.

hook.text: "Not (A and B)" equals "not A or not B." Augustus De Morgan found the swap rule that simplifies everything.

buildup.text: De Morgan's first law: ¬(P ∧ Q) ≡ (¬P ∨ ¬Q). Negate AND, distribute, flip to OR.

discovery.text: Second law: ¬(P ∨ Q) ≡ (¬P ∧ ¬Q). Negate OR, distribute, flip to AND. Mirror image of the first.

twist.text: Programmers use De Morgan constantly. Simplifying complex conditions makes code easier to read and debug.

climax.text: These two laws let you rewrite any negated compound statement into a simpler equivalent form.

punchline.text: Negate and flip: AND becomes OR.

quiz.question: What does ¬(P ∧ Q) equal according to De Morgan's laws?
